lesson.text: Quick memory: what does a bank pay you for saving? (Interest.) Banks earn that money by lending. Today: borrowing: why people do it, what it costs, and how to borrow wisely.
To borrow is to use someone else's money now and pay it back later. People borrow for big things, like a home or a business, that would take years to save for. Money borrowed is called a loan.
Borrowing usually costs money. A lender charges interest: extra paid back on top. Borrow 100 gold at 10% for a year and you pay back 100 + 10 = 110 gold. The longer you borrow, the more it can cost.
Loans are often paid back in equal parts, called repayments, each month. A 240-gold loan paid back over 12 months is 240 ÷ 12 = 20 gold a month. Missing a repayment can mean extra charges.
A credit card is a kind of borrowing: the bank pays the shop, and you pay the bank later. Paid in full on time, it costs nothing extra; money left unpaid grows with interest.
Before borrowing, ask: Do I need it now? Could I save for it instead? Can I make every repayment, even if something goes wrong? Only borrow what you are sure you can pay back.
Borrowing from friends is borrowing too. Agree clearly how much and when it will be paid back, and keep your promise. Never borrow in secret, and never from strangers online.
Try it in the world: lend a friend 10 blocks of wood and agree they will return 11 in three days. Write the deal on a sign, then check it is kept. Next: caring for the planet together.

exercises.hint: You use it now and return it later.
choices: money borrowed that must be paid back
exercises.explain: A loan is money borrowed that must be paid back.
True: lenders charge interest, extra paid back on top.

exercises.prompt: What is the extra paid back on a loan called?
exercises.hint: Savers earn it; borrowers pay it.
exercises.explain: Interest: the extra a lender charges on top of what you borrowed.

exercises.prompt: You should borrow as much as you can.
exercises.hint: What if you cannot pay it back?
exercises.explain: False: only borrow what you need and are sure you can pay back.

exercises.prompt: Before borrowing, what should you ask yourself?
exercises.hint: What matters most about a loan?
choices: Can I pay it all back?
exercises.explain: Can I pay it all back, even if something goes wrong?

exercises.prompt: Tilly borrows 200 gold at 10% for a year. How much must she pay back?
exercises.hint: Find the interest, then add it to what she borrowed.

exercises.prompt: A 360-gold loan is paid back in 12 equal monthly parts. How much is each part?
Sort these: wise or unwise borrowing?
items: borrowing only what you can repay
borrowing for a treat every day
saving up instead when you can
exercises.hint: Would it leave you able to pay everything back safely?
exercises.explain: Wise: only what you can repay, a clear date, saving instead. Unwise: daily treats, strangers online.

exercises.prompt: When does a credit card cost nothing extra?
exercises.hint: Interest grows on money left unpaid.
choices: when it is paid in full on time
exercises.explain: When the whole amount is paid back on time.

exercises.prompt: Missing a repayment can add extra charges.
exercises.hint: Lenders want to be paid on time.
exercises.explain: True: late or missed repayments can cost extra.

exercises.prompt: Loan A: pay back 110 gold. Loan B: pay back 12 parts of 10 gold. Both lend 100 gold. Which costs less?
exercises.hint: Work out Loan B's total first.
exercises.explain: Loan B: 12 × 10 = 120 gold. Loan A: 110 gold. Loan A costs 10 gold less.

exercises.prompt: Bram borrowed 50 gold and paid back 60 gold. What percentage interest did he pay?
exercises.hint: Find the extra, then how much that is for every 100 gold.
exercises.explain: 60 − 50 = 10 gold extra. 10 out of 50 is 20 out of 100: 20%.

exercises.prompt: Why do people often borrow to buy a home?
exercises.hint: How much does a home cost compared with a year's pay?
choices: it would take many years to save for
exercises.explain: A home costs so much that saving for it would take many years.

exercises.prompt: A friend lends you 5 gold. What should you do?
exercises.hint: Borrowing from friends is still borrowing.
choices: agree when to pay back, and keep your word
exercises.explain: Agree when you will pay it back, and keep your promise.

exercises.prompt: A loan of 300 gold costs 15% interest for a year. How much interest is that?
